subject: Dedicated deployment: GPU fitment scenarios for Kestrel Therapeutics
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@kestreltx.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: Kestrel Procurement <procurement@kestreltx.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU guidance for upcoming pilot

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Kestrel is moving toward a small Dedicated deployment for a pilot (Q3). We attached a high-level workload summary (kestrel_workload_summary.xlsx) but wanted a concise recommendation from Redwood on the best GPU SKU mix for our needs. Some quick context: 

- Two primary workloads: (1) high-throughput embedding and short-chat features (low latency, many small requests), (2) research workflows that run long-context generation and few-shot fine-tuning inference (long sequences, large KV state).
- Expected steady-state: ~300 req/s for embeddings peak, 2–4 concurrent long-context sessions (~32k tokens).
- Data residency: US only.
- Procurement asks: ballpark unit cost delta between H100/A100/L4, memory limits we should watch for, and HA/topology suggestions for DR.

Can you propose a recommended SKU mix and high-level rationale? We need this to finalize the procurement budget and scope the Dedicated capacity order.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Connors
Head of AI Platform
Kestrel Therapeutics

Attachments: kestrel_workload_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@kestreltx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-31T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance for upcoming pilot

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear summary and the attached workbook. High level recommendation up front: for a pilot of the size you describe, we typically recommend a heterogeneous pool rather than betting on a single SKU. Suggested starting point (pilot topology):

- L4-heavy front tier for embedding/high-throughput endpoints: 6 x L4 (for cost-efficient token throughput and embeddings). L4s are the lowest cost per token for short-context workloads and auto-scale well.
- A100 units for mixed workloads and batch-heavy experiments: 2 x A100 (40GB) to handle balanced throughput and medium-length contexts with reasonable memory headroom.
- H100 units reserved for the long-context research sessions and few-shot traces: 1 x H100 (80GB) for the ~32k token sessions and larger KV caches.

Rationale in one line: use L4 where memory is not the primary constraint and you need high concurrent throughput; keep a small fleet of A100s for general-purpose model variants; reserve H100 capacity for peak memory / long-context inference where KV-cache size and FP performance matter.

Tradeoffs / notes:
- Memory: H100 gives the largest model memory and best perf for 32k-context models; A100 (40GB) can fit many 16k models and some 32k variants sharded, but will require model/quantization tuning. L4s are limited in host memory but are efficient for 8k and smaller contexts or quantized embeddings.
- Latency vs cost: L4s are lowest cost; if you need single-digit ms for short requests at scale, increase L4 count and tune batching/caching.
- Failover: configure model routing so embedding endpoints failover from L4 -> A100 -> H100 in that order for degraded performance but preserved availability.

Operational suggestions (pilot phase):
- Autoscale L4s aggressively by request rate; set conservative cold-start bounds for A100/H100 to avoid prewarming costs.
- KV/prefix caching: enable aggressive prefix caching for chat flows on H100 to reduce repeated compute for long sessions.
- Model variants: provide a 8k quantized variant for L4s and unquantized 32k variants for H100.

I've attached a short HA topology sketch (proposed_ha_topologies.pdf) — Marissa, Ben: please weigh in on the memory and slot sizing numbers below and confirm PCIe/BW cautions.

If this direction sounds reasonable we'll put together a simple cost/latency model matching Kestrel's expected QPS and expected month-1 throughput. Would you like that as an itemized table or a 1-page summary for procurement?

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_ha_topologies.pdf (diagram, 350KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@kestreltx.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU guidance for upcoming pilot

Adding some ops/engineering detail for procurement to consider — internal notes copied to Sarah for transparency.

Key sizing calculations (pilot scope):
- Embedding throughput: 300 req/s peak -> target 99th latency < 100ms. For L4s we assume steady-state batching efficiency (avg tokens per req = 128) -> each L4 ~50–60 req/s at 100ms depending on batching window. 6 x L4 provides ~300–360 req/s headroom.
- Long-context sessions: 3–4 concurrent 32k sessions. H100 with 80GB nominal can host 2–3 concurrent large-context inference workers depending on model and kv cache sizes; recommend H100 be pinned to the research cluster with autoscale policy set to maintain at least one hot node.
- A100s: useful for background batch jobs (reranking, offline evals), and as a safety net for embedding overflow. 2 x A100 (40GB) with prewarmed model instances is a practical compromise.

Constraints and caveats:
- PCIe topology: if you're using multi-GPU nodes, ensure NVLink topologies and host memory are considered; sharded 32k contexts on A100 will require careful kernel/genesis tuning and may not hit production SLOs without extra memory.
- Quantization: L4 performance assumes int8/ql4 quantization for embedding models. If you plan to run unquantized research models on L4, expect big slowdowns.
- DR/HA: recommend a minimal cross-AZ pair topology with active L4 pool in primary AZ and warm A100/H100 pool in secondary with fast failover routes. See proposed_ha_topologies.pdf for visuals.

Action items for the proposal:
1) Alex: produce cost vs latency table (L4/A100/H100) for the expected QPS and 3-month projected usage.
2) Ben: confirm lead times and minimum order units for Dedicated SKU reservation.
3) Lauren: draft a short Procurement blurb describing the SKU mix and fallback rules to include in their PO.

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
